page: Microsoft Azure E2pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an arm64-based Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core topology, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. Storage includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD disk alongside support for Azure Premium Storage, operating with zero discrete GPUs on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.

Benchmark results display balanced single-threaded execution alongside constrained multi-threaded capacity reflecting the low core count. In single-core metrics, stress-ng recorded 2074.68 and Geekbench reached 1673.0, both placing within average performance tiers, complemented by strong gzip single-threaded compression throughput of 32.86 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics like Geekbench multi-core (3061.0) and stress-ng multi-core (4125.38) rank in weaker quartiles due to the two-core limit. PassMark aggregate CPU performance registered at 2010.78, reflecting the lack of advanced vector extensions like AVX-512. Memory benchmarks show average large-block uncached read speeds of 45.87 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 2525.57, though write speeds and cached block transfers align with lower percentiles.

From an efficiency standpoint, the ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture delivers favorable energy and resource utilization for lightweight memory-bound operations. The integrated 118 GB local NVMe SSD provides low-latency temporary scratch space without requiring immediate external disk attach fees. However, compute-bound parallel workloads face clear scaling limits due to the dual-core boundary. Microsoft Azure E2pds_v6 is technically suited for small in-memory caches, lightweight database replicas, staging microservices, Redis key-value stores, and general-purpose ARM application testing.
